timeline_reviews.summary: Top-level transport trajectory contained no projected semantic events; raw agent session files carried the actionable semantic content.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a complete installable sqlparse package with parser, formatter, splitter, CLI, public root exports, version string, tests, and packaging.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The root owned final implementation and verification, while delegating submit-tool discovery and upstream-package inspection; the inspection child also spawned source and packaging children that later wrote the workspace.
parallel.implementation: It copied upstream sqlparse sources, added wrapper modules and public exports, patched `formatter.format_sql`, adjusted packaging, experimented with the `USER` keyword then reverted it after test failures, and used a local backend shim.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through direct shared `/workspace` writes by the root and nested children, then the root finalized a complete workspace artifact that passed official evaluation.
parallel.verification: The run used repeated `pytest -q`, editable install, `python -m sqlparse --help`, and API smoke checks; official evaluation later passed all 461 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task failure remained at official closure, but the shared-workspace coordination produced redundant edits, an observed `pyproject.toml` collision, and patch rework.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same installable sqlparse requirement set, including package files, pyproject metadata, root API exports, formatting entrypoints, tests, and CLI behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned discovery, implementation, packaging, verification, and final delivery without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: It cloned upstream sqlparse, archived it into the workspace, added README and flake8 support, patched root exports, `formatter.format_sql`, version and packaging metadata, and added a public API test.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All integration occurred in one serial workspace timeline, so the edited source and packaging state had one owner and no cross-agent merge point.
serial.verification: The serial run passed the visible pytest suite, editable install, API smoke check, and `python -m sqlparse --version`; official evaluation later passed all 461 tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task failure remained at official closure; the agent reported only that the in-session submit hook was unavailable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel targeted the required full sqlparse package, public APIs, CLI, examples, tests, pyproject, and version compatibility.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial targeted the same full sqlparse package requirements and checked the upstream package before patching.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement misunderstanding; the difference was that parallel delegated requirement/source discovery while serial kept it local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across a root owner, a submit-check child, an upstream-inspection child, and nested source/packaging inspectors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation, packaging, and verification under one actor, with protocol validation showing zero spawn calls and zero child threads.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had distributed investigation and duplicate implementation activity; serial had simpler ownership with no child handoff or workspace co-ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received broad upstream/source/packaging scopes and acted through shared workspace side effects rather than a clear read-only inspection contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the full prompt and discovered upstream/packaging facts in one context, so no handoff interface had to be reconciled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context boundary let nested inspection agents write implementation files; serial avoided that cross-agent interface problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied upstream sqlparse, added wrapper modules and compatibility tests, patched packaging, tried and reverted a keyword change, and included additional files such as parser/splitter/config shims.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied upstream sqlparse, patched root exports, `formatter.format_sql`, pyproject, README, flake8, and a public API test without the extra wrapper-module layer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations were upstream-based and passed, but parallel produced a larger compatibility layer and more experimental edits than serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received the submit-check result and upstream-inspection result, but one nested packaging child was interrupted and another nested child completed after doing direct workspace edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; all discoveries, edits, and final response happened in the single main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child lifecycle management and one interrupted nested child; serial had no join or interruption risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integration occurred through a shared `/workspace`; a nested child explicitly detected a concurrent `pyproject.toml` change and re-applied packaging settings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial patched the same package metadata and API surfaces from one actor and then verified the resulting workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a same-file shared-state collision and rework; serial had a linear integration path without cross-agent file interference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel repeatedly ran pytest, editable install, CLI help, and API smoke checks before the official evaluator passed 461 of 461 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran pytest, editable install, API smoke, and CLI version checks before the official evaluator passed 461 of 461 tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached strong local and official acceptance; parallel spent extra verification cycles after duplicate/conflicting edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed 614.172 agent seconds, five subagents, and many more tool calls before finalizing after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed 199.521 agent seconds, zero subagents, and fewer tool calls before finalizing after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was substantially more expensive and longer-running, but not budget-exhausted; serial reached the same official pass more directly.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status evaluations pass 461 of 461 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is process shape, not final correctness. The serial run performed one controlled upstream import, compatibility patch, and verification sequence. The parallel run delegated inspection and submit discovery, then nested children also edited the shared project while the root was implementing, which produced a same-file `pyproject.toml` reconciliation episode and extra verification, but the root still delivered a complete passing package.
parallel_contributors: Vendored upstream sqlparse behavior and added prompt-specific API/package shims.
Delegated investigation found the unavailable submit hook and upstream release details.
Shared workspace edits caused rework but did not prevent final local or official acceptance.
serial_contributors: Single-threaded ownership kept implementation, packaging, and verification in one coherent workspace state.
Copied upstream source and made only targeted compatibility edits before local and official acceptance.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added extra wrapper modules and tests that the serial solution did not need for official success.
Parallel briefly tried changing `USER` keyword classification and reverted after visible test failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; one parallel coordination defect was adverse but not outcome-differential
